q.s: The so-called 'college of priests' of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
q.x: The 'college of priests' is a large building near the Great Bath in the citadel of Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Fire altars of the Harappan period have been found at which of the following sites?
q.x: Fire altars are reported from Kalibangan, along with Lothal, Banawali and Rakhigarhi.

q.s: The bronze image of a 'dancing girl' of the Harappan civilisation was found at:
q.x: Both the bronze dancing girl and the steatite 'priest-king' bust come from Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Which Harappan site has yielded a Persian Gulf (button) seal?
q.x: Lothal, the Harappan port in Gujarat, has yielded a Persian Gulf seal, attesting its sea trade.

q.s: Which Harappan site was almost wholly a craft town and a major bead-making centre?
q.x: Chanhudaro in Sindh had no citadel and was mainly a craft town known for bead-making.

q.s: What chiefly enabled the Later Vedic people to clear the forests of the Ganga plain for farming?
q.x: Iron axes and ploughshares, spreading in North India from about 1000 BC, made forest clearance possible.

q.s: Cemetery H, belonging to the Late Harappan phase, is associated with:
q.x: Cemetery H and Cemetery R-37 are both at Harappa; Cemetery H is Late Harappan.

q.s: The Nasik Prashasti, which calls Gautamiputra Satakarni 'Ekabrahmana', was issued by:
q.x: The Nasik inscription was issued by his mother Gautami Balasri.

q.s: Which inscription is the first to use the term 'Andhrapatha'?
q.x: The Maidavolu plates of the Pallava Sivaskandavarma first use the term 'Andhrapatha'.

q.s: The Gandhara Grave culture, with horse remains and new burial forms, is found mainly in the:
q.x: The Gandhara Grave culture lies in the Swat valley of the north-west.

q.s: The Rig Vedic river 'Shutudri' is identified with the:
q.x: Shutudri is the Sutlej; Vipas is the Beas, Parushni the Ravi and Asikni the Chenab.

q.s: The Vedic river 'Sadanira' is identified with the modern:
q.x: Sadanira of the Satapatha Brahmana is the Gandak; Drishadvati is the Chautang.

q.s: Which Vedic assembly vanished altogether in the Later Vedic age?
q.x: The Vidatha disappeared, while the Sabha and Samiti survived but came under chiefs and nobles.

q.s: The earliest statement of the four varnas is found in the:
q.x: The Purusha Sukta of the Tenth Mandala of the Rigveda first names the four varnas.

q.s: The form of marriage in which the daughter was given to the officiating priest as his fee was called:
q.x: Daiva marriage gave the daughter to the priest; in Arsha the groom gave a token cow and bull.

q.s: Which of the following was regarded as the lowest form of marriage?
q.x: Paishacha, the seduction of a sleeping or drunk girl, was the lowest of the eight forms.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three marks of existence in Buddhism?
q.x: The three marks are Anicca (impermanence), Anatta (non-self) and Dukkha (suffering); Nirvana is the goal.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Mahavamsa was written by Ashvaghosha.
The Avadanashataka is written in Pali.
The Buddhacharita is written in Sanskrit.
The Vinayavatthu is a Jain text.
q.x: Ashvaghosha's Buddhacharita is in Sanskrit; the Avadanashataka is also Sanskrit, the Mahavamsa is by Mahanama and the Vinayavatthu is Buddhist.

q.s: The Madhyamika school of Buddhism was founded by:
q.x: Nagarjuna, with Aryadeva, founded the Madhyamika; Asanga and Vasubandhu are linked with Yogachara.

q.s: The Yogachara (Vijnanavada) school of Buddhism is associated with:
q.x: Yogachara was developed by Maitreyanatha, Asanga and Vasubandhu.

q.s: Ashoka sent the missionaries Sona and Uttara to:
q.x: Sona and Uttara went to Suvarnabhumi; Majjhantika went to Kashmir and Gandhara.

q.s: The Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda is linked with the reign of which Ikshvaku king?
q.x: The Maha Chaitya was built in the reign of Veerapurushadatta.

q.s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam lies on the bank of the river:
q.x: Salihundam in Srikakulam district is on the Vamsadhara.

q.s: Salihundam was brought to light in 1919 by:
q.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy discovered the site in 1919; it is known for bronze images of Tara.

q.s: The Mauryan king Bindusara is identified with which name used by Greek writers?
q.x: Amitrochates is the Greek form of his title Amitraghata ('slayer of foes'); Sandrocottus is Chandragupta.

q.s: Which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka names the Andhras among the peoples following his Dhamma?
q.x: Rock Edict XIII, which describes the Kalinga war, also names the Andhras.

q.s: Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts are written mainly in which language?
q.x: They are in Prakrit, mostly in Brahmi script, with Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic in the north-west.

q.s: The gold coins of Chandragupta II were called:
q.x: Gupta gold coins were dinaras; the silver coins were rupakas.

q.s: Gupta administration was more decentralised than the Mauryan because:
o: Much of the empire was held by feudatories and officials were paid in land
Provinces were ruled only by royal princes
The emperor had no standing army
q.x: The Guptas relied on samantas and land grants, unlike the centrally regulated Mauryan state.

q.s: The Sarnath school of Gupta sculpture used:
q.x: Sarnath images were carved in polished Chunar buff sandstone; Mathura used spotted red sandstone.

q.s: The Sultanganj Buddha, a large Gupta-period metal image, was found in:
q.x: It comes from Sultanganj near Bhagalpur in Bihar.

q.s: Rajaraja I directed the sabhas of Cholamandalam to serve which temple?
q.x: Rajaraja I built the Brihadeshvara temple and tied village sabhas to its service.

q.s: Which Chola ruler abolished tolls and was called 'Sungam Tavirtta Chola'?
q.x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls (sungam).

q.s: The great land survey of the Chola empire (1001 CE) is associated with:
q.x: Rajaraja I ordered the great survey of land for revenue.

q.s: Which ruler of Ranthambore was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301?
q.x: Hammir Deva Chauhan held Ranthambore; Ratan Singh ruled Chittor and Rai Karan Gujarat.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, 'jizya' was:
o: A land tax on Muslim landholders
q.x: Jizya was levied on non-Muslims in place of military service; zakat was the religious tax on Muslims.

q.s: The term 'khums' in the medieval tax system refers to:
q.x: Khums was the state's one-fifth of war booty; haqq-e-sharb was the irrigation tax.

q.s: The du-aspa sih-aspa system in the mansabdari was introduced by:
q.x: Jahangir introduced du-aspa sih-aspa, allowing a mansabdar to maintain extra horsemen.

q.s: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the 'sawar' rank indicated the:
o: Number of cavalrymen to be maintained
q.x: Zat fixed personal rank and pay; sawar fixed the number of horsemen.

q.s: The title 'Asaf Jah' was conferred on Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1725 by:
q.x: Muhammad Shah gave him the title Asaf Jah; Farrukhsiyar had given 'Nizam-ul-Mulk'.

q.s: In 1724 Nizam-ul-Mulk defeated the Mughal governor Mubariz Khan at the battle of:
q.x: Shakar Kheda (1724) laid the foundation of the independent Hyderabad State.

q.s: Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union in 1948 through:
q.x: Operation Polo (September 1948) ended the Nizam's rule.

q.s: Osmania University was founded by:
q.x: The seventh and last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan, founded Osmania University.

q.s: 'Fall of the Mughal Empire' was written by:
q.x: Jadunath Sarkar wrote it; M. Athar Ali wrote The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb.

q.s: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's father Maha Singh was the chief of which misl?
q.x: Ranjit Singh, born at Gujranwala in 1780, belonged to the Sukerchakia misl.

q.s: From whom did Ranjit Singh obtain the Kohinoor diamond in 1813?
q.x: The Afghan ruler Shah Shuja handed over the Kohinoor in 1813.

q.s: The Treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon between the Marathas and the Nizam followed the battle of:
q.x: Baji Rao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed in 1728, leading to Mungi-Shevgaon.

q.s: In 1610 the Portuguese lost Pulicat to the:
q.x: The Dutch took Pulicat in 1610 and made it their Coromandel headquarters.

q.s: Jhansi was recaptured by the British in April 1858 under:
q.x: Hugh Rose took Jhansi in April 1858 and Gwalior in June 1858.

q.s: Which British officer was killed during the recapture of Delhi in September 1857?
q.x: John Nicholson led the assault on Delhi and died of his wounds.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the treaties of Allahabad (1765) is correct?
o: The Company got the Diwani of Awadh.
Shuja-ud-daula of Awadh paid a war indemnity of Rs 50 lakh.
Shah Alam II was given Bengal as his personal domain.
The Nawab of Awadh received Rs 53 lakh for the nizamat.
q.x: Shuja-ud-daula paid Rs 50 lakh and gave the Company duty-free trade in Awadh; the Rs 53 lakh for nizamat went to the Nawab of Bengal.

q.s: By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Shah Alam II granted the English Company the:
o: Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
Right to mint coins in Delhi
q.x: The Diwani, the right to collect revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, came to the Company in 1765.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
q.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance; Satara (1848), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) fell under Lapse.

q.s: Which was the first state annexed by Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse?
q.x: Satara was annexed first, in 1848.

q.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Tipu Sultan died in 1799 at Srirangapatna; 1792 was the Treaty of Srirangapatna.

q.s: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The 1892 Act came under Lansdowne; the 1861 Act under Canning.

q.s: The portfolio system in the Governor-General's council was introduced in the time of:
q.x: Canning introduced the portfolio system under the Indian Councils Act of 1861.

q.s: 'Prosperous British India' was written by:
q.x: William Digby wrote it; R.C. Dutt wrote Economic History of India.

q.s: The first passenger railway in India (1853) ran between:
q.x: The first train ran from Bombay to Thane on 16 April 1853.

q.s: 'Andhra Patrika' (1908) was founded by:
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao started it as a weekly from Bombay in 1908.

q.s: 'Krishna Patrika' (1902) was started by:
q.x: Konda Venkatappayya founded it; Mutnuri Krishna Rao later edited it.

q.s: The first Factory Act in India (1881) was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The 1881 Factory Act and the Ilbert Bill (1883) both belong to Ripon's time.

q.s: The Indian Penal Code was enacted in:
q.x: The IPC dates from 1860; the Civil Procedure Code from 1859 and the Criminal Procedure Code from 1861.

q.s: Sati was declared a crime by the Bengal Regulation of 1829 under Governor-General:
q.x: Bentinck passed Regulation XVII of 1829; Rammohan Roy led the campaign.

q.s: The Scientific Society was founded by Sayyid Ahmad Khan in 1864 at:
q.x: It was founded at Ghazipur and later shifted to Aligarh.

q.s: The Akali (Gurdwara Reform) movement sought to free the gurdwaras from:
q.x: The Akalis fought the mahants through the SGPC and the Akali Dal and won the Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

q.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, which placed the gurdwaras under the SGPC, was passed in:
q.x: The Act of 1925 was the success of the Akali movement.

q.s: Who presided over the Bombay session of the Indian National Congress in 1889?
q.x: Wedderburn presided in 1889; Alfred Webb in 1894 and Ananda Mohan Bose in 1898.

q.s: The raid on the Pahartali European Club (1932) was led by:
q.x: Pritilata Waddedar led the raid and took cyanide; Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the Comilla magistrate.

q.s: Who handed Simon a 'Simon Go Back' letter at Vijayawada railway station?
q.x: Kaleswara Rao gave the letter at Vijayawada; Prakasam led the Madras procession.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam became 'Andhra Kesari' after baring his chest to police during the anti-Simon procession at:
q.x: In the Madras procession of 1928 Prakasam faced the police after Parthasarathi was killed in firing.

q.s: Which one of the following pairs (book – author) is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Man Who Divided India – Rafiq Zakaria
Pakistan or the Partition of India – B.R. Ambedkar
q.x: The Indian Musalmans (1871) was written by W.W. Hunter.

q.s: The Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League (1940) was moved by:
q.x: Fazlul Huq moved it; Jinnah presided, Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted it and Khaliquzzaman seconded it.

q.s: Gandhi's first Satyagraha Ashram in India (1915) was set up at:
q.x: The 1915 ashram was at Kochrab, Ahmedabad; it moved to Sabarmati in 1917.

q.s: Who was the first to call Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'?
q.x: Bose used the phrase in a 1944 radio address from Singapore; Tagore called him 'Mahatma'.

q.s: The Swaraj Party, which took up council work in 1923, was founded by:
q.x: Das and Motilal Nehru led the pro-changers; Rajagopalachari led the no-changers who did constructive work.

q.s: The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at the Lahore session of the Congress in:
q.x: Lahore (Dec 1929) came after the Simon Commission (1928) and before the Dandi March and the First RTC (1930).

q.s: Jayaprakash Narayan gave the call for 'Sampoorna Kranti' (Total Revolution) in 1974 at:
q.x: JP declared it at the Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on 5 June 1974.

q.s: During the Quit India Movement, Jayaprakash Narayan escaped in November 1942 from:
q.x: JP escaped from Hazaribagh Jail on Diwali night, 1942.

q.s: Subhas Chandra Bose's presidential address calling for a planning commission was delivered at which Congress session?
q.x: The Haripura address is a milestone in Indian planning.

q.s: The Royal Indian Navy mutiny of February 1946 broke out at:
q.x: It began on HMIS Talwar at Bombay and, with the INA trials, showed the forces' loyalty could no longer be relied on.

q.s: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Boundary Commission(s) for:
q.x: Radcliffe chaired both commissions; the award was ready on 12 August and published on 17 August 1947.

q.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 received royal assent on:
q.x: The Bill was introduced on 4 July and received assent on 18 July 1947.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Constituent Assemblies to act as legislatures
Retention of the Secretary of State for India
q.x: The Act abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India.

q.s: The Chirala-Perala movement of 1921 was led by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya (Andhra Ratna) led the people out to Ramnagar.

q.s: The people of Chirala-Perala left their homes in 1921 in protest against:
o: Heavy tax after the towns were made a municipality
q.x: The yearly tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000 when the municipality was formed.

q.s: Pingali Venkayya was called 'Patti Venkayya' because of his research on:
q.x: His work on cotton, especially Cambodia cotton, earned the name Patti (cotton) Venkayya.

q.s: Gandhi founded the Natal Indian Congress in:
q.x: He reached South Africa in 1893 and founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.

q.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was passed in:
q.x: The Madras Estates Act is of 1948; the Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation of 1949.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Andhra High Court at Guntur?
q.x: Koka Subba Rao, later Chief Justice of India, was the first Chief Justice at Guntur.

q.s: The first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly (1956) was:
q.x: Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of AP; Nallapati Venkatramaiah had been Speaker of Andhra State.

q.s: 'Swami Sitaram', who fasted for 35 days at Guntur in 1951 for a separate Andhra State, was:
q.x: Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri was known as Swami Sitaram.

q.s: On whose appeal did Swami Sitaram end his fast in 1951?
q.x: He ended the fast on Vinoba Bhave's appeal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Andhra movement is correct?
o: Krishna and Guntur were its keenest supporters.
Rayalaseema was its strongest supporter from the start.
The surplus revenue of the Tamil areas was spent on the Andhra deltas.
It opposed a port at Visakhapatnam.
q.x: Krishna and Guntur led; Rayalaseema and Nellore were lukewarm, the delta surplus went to Tamil areas, and a Vizag port was an early demand.

q.s: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: NTR of the TDP became CM in 1983.

q.s: Who had the shortest tenure (31 days) as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was CM from 16 August to 16 September 1984.

q.s: The microlithic tool centres of Andhra were discovered by:
q.x: Robert Bruce Foote, the father of Indian prehistory, found them.

q.s: The Jogalthambi hoard contains silver coins of which ruler, restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni?
q.x: About 13,270 coins of the Kshaharata Nahapana were restruck after Gautamiputra defeated him.

q.s: Which Satavahana king performed two Ashvamedhas and was a contemporary of Kharavela?
q.x: Satakarni I, known from the Naneghat inscription of Nayanika, performed two Ashvamedhas.

q.s: The Prakrit anthology Gathasaptasati is attributed to which Satavahana king?
q.x: Hala, the 17th king of the Matsya list, is credited with the Gathasaptasati.

q.s: The Rashtrakuta capital Manyakheta was built by:
q.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta (Malkhed, Karnataka); the early seat was Elapura (Ellora).

q.s: The 'Bhimeswara Puranam' on the Draksharama temple was written by:
q.x: Srinatha wrote the Bhimeswara Puranam.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Trilinga kshetras?
q.x: The Trilinga kshetras are Srisailam, Kaleswaram and Draksharama; Samalkot is the twin Bhimeswara temple.

q.s: In the battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya defeated the:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah at Raichur in 1520.

q.s: In 1323 the Kakatiya king Prataparudra was captured by:
q.x: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq) captured him; Kafur's 1309-10 raid had made him a tributary.

q.s: The Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava (Sevuna) ruler:
q.x: Rudramadevi defeated Mahadeva when he besieged Warangal.

q.s: The Nayankara system, later carried on by the Vijayanagara rulers, originated under the:
q.x: Vijayanagara adopted the Kakatiya Nayankara system of military land assignments.

q.s: The Adina Mosque at Pandua was built by the Bengal Sultan:
q.x: Sikandar Shah built the Adina Mosque (1373-75); Ilyas Shah had unified Bengal in 1342.

q.s: Sayana, the famous commentator on the Vedas, was the brother of:
q.x: Sayana was Vidyaranya's (Madhava's) brother; the commentaries were begun under Bukka I.

q.s: Kakatiya temple architecture belongs to which style?
q.x: The Kakatiyas, once feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, took over the Vesara idiom.

q.s: The Vellore Mutiny broke out in:
q.x: It broke out on 10 July 1806, about half a century before 1857.

q.s: Which Governor of Madras was recalled after the Vellore Mutiny?
q.x: William Bentinck and Commander-in-Chief Cradock were recalled.

q.s: Who published the 'Verses of Vemana' in 1829?
q.x: C.P. Brown published Vemana's verses in 1829.

q.s: The description of Telugu as the 'Italian of the East' is traced to:
q.x: The phrase is first traced to the Venetian traveller Nicolo de Conti.

q.s: The Rajahmundry College incident of 1907 followed the visit of:
q.x: Students wore Vandemataram badges after Pal's visit; Gadicherla presented an address to Pal.

q.s: The earliest of the Hindu Nataka Samajams (1880-81) was founded at:
q.x: Guntur (1880-81) came first, then Kakinada (1885) and Rajahmundry (1889).

q.s: The Telugu monthly 'Andhra Mahila' was run by:
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh ran Andhra Mahila.

q.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao funded his public work from the business of:
q.x: He founded Amrutanjan and used its income for Andhra Patrika and Andhra Granthamala.

q.s: 'Bhumi Panduga', ending with the Kommu dance, is a festival of the:
q.x: Bhumi Panduga is the Koya festival before monsoon sowing; Seethala Panduga is Lambadi.

q.s: The Surabhi theatre company was founded in 1885 in Surabhi village of which district?
q.x: Vanarasa Govinda Rao and his brother founded it in Kadapa district.

q.s: The Praja Rajyam Party founded by Chiranjeevi merged in 2011 with the:
q.x: It merged with the Congress and Chiranjeevi became Union MoS (IC) for Tourism.

q.s: The movement of societies 'from status to contract' was described by:
q.x: Henry Maine wrote of the shift from status to contract in Ancient Law.

q.s: Under Muslim personal law, 'Khula' is a divorce at the instance of the:
q.x: Khula is initiated by the wife; mubarat is by mutual consent.

q.s: Talaq pronounced three times at one sitting is known as:
q.x: Talaq-e-Biddat is instant triple talaq; Talaq-e-Hasan is spread over three months.

q.s: The fusion of distinct groups and cultures into a new one is called:
q.x: In acculturation a group stays distinct; peaceful coexistence of groups is cultural pluralism.

q.s: The idea of 'status inconsistency' in stratification is associated with:
q.x: Lenski spoke of status inconsistency; Davis and Moore gave the functional theory.

q.s: The Indira Gandhi National Tribal University (2007) at Amarkantak is in:
q.x: Amarkantak is in Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (1999) was carved out of the Ministry of:
q.x: It was formed in 1999 from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

q.s: In ancient India, the custom of 'niyoga' allowed:
o: A childless widow to bear a son by a kinsman
A widow to remarry outside the caste
A girl to choose her husband in an assembly
A wife to divorce her husband
q.x: Niyoga was levirate for a son; it did not ban remarriage.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
q.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and binds private persons as well.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that Article 17 can be enforced against private persons?
o: Indra Sawhney v Union of India (1992)
q.x: PUDR (1982) held that Article 17 operates against private persons too.

q.s: The Special Investigation Team probing the Godhra and 2002 Gujarat riot cases was appointed by the:
q.x: The Supreme Court appointed the SIT.

q.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Verma Committee was set up after the December 2012 Delhi case.

q.s: The PENCIL portal against child labour (2017) was launched by the Ministry of:
q.x: PENCIL (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) belongs to the Labour Ministry.

q.s: A student protest against attendance rules is an example of which type of agitation?
q.x: Resistance agitations oppose a change; persuasive ones seek a specific concession such as postponing an exam; revolutionary ones seek to overthrow the system.

q.s: Which is the first stage of the public policy cycle?
q.x: The cycle runs agenda setting, formulation, adoption, implementation, evaluation and termination or revision.

q.s: Which body is the nodal agency for poverty estimation in India?
q.x: NITI Aayog estimates poverty using NSO consumption survey data.

q.s: Which survey is the standard source of unemployment data in India?
q.x: The PLFS is the standard for unemployment data; HCES measures consumption.

q.s: The 'Ujjawala' scheme (2007) of the Ministry of Women and Child Development is related to:
o: Prevention of trafficking and rehabilitation of victims
q.x: Ujjawala is an anti-trafficking scheme, now part of Shakti Sadan; PM Ujjwala Yojana (2016) gives LPG connections.

q.s: Which State set up India's first Transgender Welfare Board in 2008?
q.x: Tamil Nadu had the first welfare board; Kerala had the first State transgender policy (2015).

q.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: NREP was launched in 1980; RLEGP came in 1983.

q.s: Under the PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana, the pension of Rs 3,000 a month begins at the age of:
q.x: The pension starts at 60.

q.s: PM-KISAN provides eligible farmer families an income support of:
o: Rs 12,000 a year in four instalments
Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments
Rs 10,000 a year in two instalments
q.x: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme covering all landholding farmer families since 2019.

q.s: The Weaker Section Housing Programme in Andhra Pradesh, with the motto 'Housing for All', is run by the:
o: AP Urban Infrastructure Asset Management Ltd
q.x: The AP State Housing Corporation runs it.

q.s: Before its 2021-22 term, India's previous term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council was in:
q.x: India's 2011-12 term was its seventh; 2021-22 its eighth.

q.s: Which permanent member of the UN Security Council opposes India's claim to a permanent seat?
q.x: France, Russia, the UK and the US back India's claim; China opposes it.

q.s: Who succeeded David Malpass as President of the World Bank in June 2023?
q.x: Ajay Banga became World Bank President in 2023.

q.s: Who has been the Managing Director of the IMF since October 2019?
q.x: Georgieva succeeded Lagarde in 2019.

q.s: In BIMSTEC, India is the lead country for which sector?
q.x: After the sectors were cut from 14 to 7, India leads security; Thailand leads connectivity.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a full member of the Colombo Security Conclave?
q.x: Seychelles is an observer; the Conclave began in 2011 as an India-Sri Lanka-Maldives trilateral and has its secretariat at Colombo.

q.s: 'Operation Cactus' (1988) was carried out by India in:
q.x: Indian forces foiled a coup against President Gayoom in the Maldives.

q.s: The Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), India's external intelligence agency, works under the:
